criteria.criterion: The producer brief built in crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs tells the producer to run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` on its changed files before finishing and to reword any banned word found; a unit test asserts this text is in the producer brief.
criteria.evidence: briefs.rs adds BOUNDARY_SCAN_INSTRUCTION ("Before you finish, run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` on your changed files... Reword any banned word it finds, then run it again until it passes") to banned_words_section. The test producer_briefs_tell_the_producer_to_run_the_boundary_scan checks the text is present and sits between '## Words you must not write' and '## Checks Athena will run'. It passed when I ran it.

criteria.criterion: A new test shows a request text containing a banned boundary word (built from fragments) is flagged before admission with the word and its location, while a clean request passes. Run `cargo test` and see the test pass.
criteria.evidence: a_request_with_a_banned_word_is_refused_before_admission_and_a_clean_one_is_admitted builds the word from ["oper","ator"]. It checks that both ask and queue fail with 'not admitted' and 'request:2: <word>', that HEAD does not move, and that the reworded request is admitted and HEAD moves. Without refuse_banned_input, ask would succeed and unwrap_err would panic, so the test fails without the change. It passed when I ran it, and the recorded full `cargo test --locked` passed.

criteria.criterion: A new test shows a file named in the request that contains a banned word is flagged before admission, with its path and line, and a clean named file is not. Run `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: a_named_file_with_a_banned_word_is_flagged_with_path_and_line_and_a_clean_one_is_not commits docs/dirty.md, which holds a word built from fragments, and checks that ask fails with 'docs/dirty.md:3: <word>' and that HEAD does not move. It also checks that scan_request_input returns only the dirty-file finding (the clean file gives none and a missing path is skipped), and that a request naming docs/clean.md is admitted. It passed when I ran it.

findings.summary: A changed file is outside the expected deliverables list
findings.evidence: The diff changes docs/enforcement.md (the M19 row of the enforcement map), and that file is not on the deliverables list. The edit is accurate, documents the new mechanism, and every test it names exists (every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists passed).

findings.summary: The scan also blocks requests Athena generates itself, which no person can reword
findings.evidence: queue() is also called by hestia's error review and backfill, and by code_health. hestia's root_cause_request copies the introspection cause and its proposed prevention from records, which is agent free text. If those quote a banned word, which is likely when the repeated failure is itself a boundary-scan failure like job a5sf, the queue call now fails: try_error_review reports 'could not run', and apply_step returns an error for the backfill pass. I found this by reading the code; I did not exercise it, and no test covers it.

findings.summary: The admission scan does not skip owner files, which the policy scan excludes
findings.evidence: The policy scan reads athena_files(), which leaves out owner files. scan_request_input skips only records/ and LICENSE, so a request naming an owner file that holds a banned word would be refused even though the policy scan accepts that file. Found by reading the code.

summary: The change does what was asked. The producer brief now tells the producer to run `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` and reword any banned word it finds, and a unit test checks that text is there. `athena ask` and `athena ask --later` (`queue`) now scan the request text, and every file the request names, with a new `boundary_scan` in athena-context. That scan reuses the brief's word lists, which an existing test keeps equal to the policy scanner's lists, so there is no third copy. If the scan finds a banned word, Athena refuses the request, lists each hit as `source:line: word`, and edits nothing. A new policy test checks that the admission scan and the policy scan flag exactly the same lines. I ran all the new tests and they pass (`the_admission_scan_finds_what_the_policy_scan_finds` with the full policy suite). The recorded fmt, clippy and full test runs passed. I found three minor issues and no blockers. First, docs/enforcement.md changed but is not on the deliverables list. Second, the scan also runs on requests Athena queues itself (hestia root-cause requests, code-health passes). Those can quote recorded agent text and cannot be reworded by a person, so a repeated failure about a banned word could stop its own root-cause request from being queued. I found this by reading the code; no test exercises it. Third, the admission scan does not skip owner files, which the policy scan excludes.
